title: HBOD: on-device application, state-space engine and simulation code
description:
HBOD (Hooper-Borg-Oslo-Dergaa) is an autonomous artificial intelligence agent for daily monitoring of training load, wellness and health. This release matches the paper Development of an autonomous artificial intelligence agent for training load monitoring: a simulation study and closed-loop in silico trial against the acute-to-chronic workload ratio.

It holds (1) the HBOD web application, which is free for academic and training use and computes on the coach's device without uploading any data; (2) its state-space engine, a Kalman filter on fitness, fatigue and wellness strain with athlete-specific learning by recursive least squares, which reports the posterior probability that the athlete's modelled state exceeds his or her own baseline (this probability is not an injury risk); (3) the complete simulation code of the paper (Supplementary File S1); and (4) the parity test of the JavaScript engine against the Python code of File S1.

The acute-to-chronic workload ratio is displayed for planning only and triggers no decision. The rule-based prototype compared in the paper is kept only as the archived earlier release v0.1.0-rule-based-prototype.

The protocol and the frozen analysis plan are registered on the Open Science Framework: https://doi.org/10.17605/OSF.IO/MUWQ3.
